text:
Early Blight (Alternaria solani) in Tomato:
Symptoms: Brown circular spots with yellow halo on older leaves, 1-2cm diameter. Concentric rings give target-board appearance.
Cause: Fungal pathogen Alternaria solani. Favoured by warm humid weather (24-29°C), excessive dew.
Treatment: Mancozeb 75 WP @ 2g/litre every 7-10 days. Copper Oxychloride 50 WP @ 3g/litre as follow-up.
Prevention: Crop rotation, remove infected leaves, avoid overhead irrigation, apply mulch.

Late Blight (Phytophthora infestans) in Potato/Tomato:
Symptoms: Water-soaked pale green spots on leaves, white cottony growth on undersides in humid conditions. Brown lesions on stems.
Cause: Oomycete pathogen. Spreads rapidly in cool wet weather (10-20°C, >90% humidity).
Treatment: Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (Ridomil Gold) @ 2.5g/litre. Dimethomorph 50 WP @ 1g/litre.
Prevention: Certified disease-free seed, adequate spacing, avoid late-evening irrigation.

Powdery Mildew in Wheat:
Symptoms: White powdery coating on leaves and stems. Causes yellowing and premature leaf death.
Cause: Blumeria graminis. Favoured by moderate temperatures (15-22°C) and high humidity.
Treatment: Propiconazole 25 EC @ 0.1% (1ml/litre). Tebuconazole 250 EW @ 1ml/litre.
Prevention: Resistant varieties like HD-2781, PBW-343. Avoid excess nitrogen.

Yellow Mosaic Virus in Soybean:
Symptoms: Interveinal chlorosis (yellow patches between veins), mottled appearance, leaf curl, stunted growth.
Cause: Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus (MYMV), transmitted by whitefly Bemisia tabaci.
Treatment: No cure for infected plants. Control whitefly with Imidacloprid 17.8 SL @ 0.5ml/litre or Thiamethoxam 25 WG @ 0.3g/litre.
Prevention: Resistant varieties (JS 335, NRC 37). Roguing infected plants. Yellow sticky traps.

Red Rot in Sugarcane:
Symptoms: Red discolouration inside stalk with white patches. Sour smell, wilting of top leaves.
Cause: Colletotrichum falcatum fungus. Spreads through infected setts and waterlogging.
Treatment: No effective chemical cure. Remove and destroy infected clumps. Treat setts with Carbendazim 50 WP @ 1g/litre before planting.
Prevention: Use disease-free setts from certified nurseries. Resistant varieties Co 86032, Co 94012.

Nitrogen Deficiency in crops:
Symptoms: Yellowing starting from older (lower) leaves moving upward. Stunted growth, pale green colour throughout plant.
Correction: Apply Urea (46% N) @ 20-25 kg/acre as top dressing. For immediate effect, foliar spray of 2% Urea solution.
Crops most affected: Maize, Rice, Wheat, Sugarcane.
Prevention: Soil test before sowing. Split nitrogen application — 50% basal, 25% at 30 DAS, 25% at 60 DAS.

Phosphorus Deficiency:
Symptoms: Purple or reddish coloration on undersides of leaves and stems. Dark green older leaves. Poor root development, delayed flowering.
Correction: Apply DAP (18:46:0) @ 100 kg/ha. Single Superphosphate (16% P2O5) @ 250 kg/ha.
Soil treatment: Rock phosphate for acidic soils. Apply with organic matter to improve availability.
Prevention: Maintain soil pH 6.0-7.0 for maximum phosphorus availability.

Aphid infestation management:
Symptoms: Clusters of small soft-bodied insects on young shoots and undersides of leaves. Sticky honeydew, sooty mould, leaf curl.
Crops affected: Wheat, Mustard, Chilli, Tomato, Cotton, Potato.
Treatment: Imidacloprid 17.8 SL @ 0.3ml/litre spray. Dimethoate 30 EC @ 2ml/litre. Neem oil 5ml/litre for organic control.
Biological control: Encourage ladybird beetles (Coccinellidae) and parasitic wasps.

Alluvial Soil characteristics and management:
Found in: Indo-Gangetic plains, river deltas. States: UP, Bihar, Punjab, Haryana, West Bengal.
Properties: High fertility, good water retention, pH 6.5-8.0. Rich in potash, poor in nitrogen and phosphorus.
Best crops: Wheat, Rice, Sugarcane, Maize, Vegetables.
Management: Regular organic matter addition, balanced NPK, avoid waterlogging.

Black Cotton Soil (Regur) characteristics:
Found in: Maharashtra, MP, Gujarat, Karnataka, AP.
Properties: High clay content (montmorillonite), swells when wet, cracks when dry. pH 7.5-8.5. Rich in calcium, magnesium, potassium. Poor in nitrogen, phosphorus, organic matter.
Best crops: Cotton, Soybean, Sorghum, Wheat, Sunflower.
Management: Deep ploughing, green manuring, gypsum for excess sodium.

Ideal soil pH ranges for major crops:
Rice: 5.5-6.5, Wheat: 6.0-7.0, Maize: 5.8-7.0, Cotton: 6.0-8.0, Soybean: 6.0-6.8, Tomato: 6.0-6.8, Potato: 4.8-5.5, Onion: 6.0-7.0, Sugarcane: 6.0-7.5.
If pH too low (acidic): Apply agricultural lime (CaCO3) @ 2-3 tonnes/ha.
If pH too high (alkaline): Apply gypsum (CaSO4) @ 5-10 tonnes/ha or elemental sulphur.

Onion price seasonality in India:
Prices typically lowest during Oct-Dec (harvest season, Rabi crop arrives). Prices peak during June-August (pre-Kharif scarcity period).
Key markets: Lasalgaon (Asia's largest onion market), Pune, Nashik, Delhi Azadpur.
Storage tip: Store in well-ventilated gunny bags at 25-35°C and <65% humidity. Losses reduced by treating with maleic hydrazide 2500ppm before harvest.
Price factors: Maharashtra production (35% of India), export demand, monsoon timing.

MSP (Minimum Support Price) policy in India:
CACP recommends MSP for 23 crops annually. Government announces before sowing season.
Kharif 2025-26 key MSPs: Paddy (Common) Rs 2300/qtl, Maize Rs 2090/qtl, Soybean Rs 4892/qtl, Cotton (Medium) Rs 7121/qtl, Groundnut Rs 6783/qtl.
Rabi 2025-26: Wheat Rs 2425/qtl, Mustard Rs 5950/qtl, Chana Rs 5650/qtl.
How to sell at MSP: Register on PM-KISAN portal, contact local APMC or FCI procurement centre.

Kharif crop calendar for India:
Sowing: June-July (with onset of monsoon). Harvest: September-October.
Major Kharif crops: Rice, Maize, Sorghum, Bajra, Cotton, Soybean, Groundnut, Turmeric, Sugarcane.
Key activities: Land preparation in May, seed treatment before sowing, top dressing at 30 and 60 DAS, pest monitoring weekly.

Rabi crop calendar for India:
Sowing: October-December. Harvest: March-April.
Major Rabi crops: Wheat, Barley, Mustard, Chana (Chickpea), Lentil, Peas, Potato.
Key activities: Deep ploughing after Kharif harvest, irrigation scheduling (6-8 irrigations for wheat), weed management at 3 weeks after sowing.
